## Install

Nothing here is code-signed yet, so your system will ask you to confirm the first time.

| | File | First time |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** | `BoardDock-2.1.0-win-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `…-portable.exe` (no install) | Choose **More info → Run anyway**. |
| **macOS** | `BoardDock-2.1.0-mac-….dmg` (open it and drag BoardDock into Applications) | Right-click the app and choose **Open**. |
| **Linux** | `BoardDock-2.1.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or the `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./BoardDock-2.1.0-linux-….deb`) | Nothing. |
| **In your browser** | [danmover.github.io/boarddock](https://danmover.github.io/boarddock) | Nothing is uploaded: it all runs in your browser. |

The desktop app does two things the browser can't: it opens Cadence Allegro `.brd` boards (with KiCad 10 or newer installed, free from kicad.org), and **Open plate** hands a plate to a slicer you have installed.

**Nothing BoardDock makes has been printed and tried yet.** Print the test-fit kit first (30 to 40 minutes), and treat anything about fit, strength and clips as coming from the model and its checks, not from a real print.

## What's new

- **J-Links and USB-serial adapters are ordinary boards.** They have their own connectors (the J-Link's is the 20-pin 1.27 mm Cortex one, with USB-B; the adapter has its six male pins and mini-USB) and are docked and cabled like any board. Old projects convert when they open, keeping their cables and ribbon lengths.
- **Small boards stack in columns.** Anything up to about 105 × 60 mm stands on its long edge, the next one on top like bricks, each holder on pegs on the one below. One release rod runs down through the whole column, and each holder lifts straight off. Auto-arrange puts a board's J-Link and adapter in a column behind it; by hand, Rails › Stacks has **Stack on…**, **Take off the stack** and **On its edge**. A column is held to what the dock's tongue can carry (in PETG a J-Link and an adapter fit; two J-Links don't, and the second gets a column of its own, with a longer ribbon).
- **Many more connectors are recognised**, by name and by part number, each drawn as itself in 3D with its own plug: Samtec SHF, TSW and FTSH headers, TE and other D-subs, Bel MagJack RJ45s, CUI DC jacks, Molex, JST and Hirose sockets, Sullins headers and more. A connector nobody has named is recognised by its pins. Names are read as Allegro libraries write them (IPC-7251 header names, a maker's name in front of a part number, part numbers with the dashes taken out), and a chip or diode that only has a connector-like word in its name (a diode package called SMA, a TRS3232, a USB4640) is no longer taken for a connector.
- **The rest of the connector families are known too:** board-to-board connectors (Samtec QSH, QTE, SEAM, ERM8; Hirose DF12, DF40; Molex SlimStack), M.2, mini PCIe, PCIe and DIMM sockets, XLR, banana jacks, M12 and M8, TOSLINK, SIM slots, SATA, SFP cages, mini-DIN, IEC C14 inlets, MMCX, MCX and SMB, and Multicomp, Weidmüller, Degson and Phoenix terminal blocks. Nothing is cabled to a socket a board or card goes on, and no cradle or cap is printed for one. A KK or JST-VH header's pins are drawn at 3.96 mm.
- **Cadence Allegro boards open in the desktop app** (through KiCad's own `kicad-cli`), and a board's debug header takes a J-Link.
- **The DC barrel jack on an Arduino takes a supply's lead** by hand, and ticking a cradle, cap, guard or tie anchor on an empty port now says you'll plug it in (nothing is printed for a port with no plug in it).
- **The Wiring view fits a big rack.** The cards take the shape of the window, so a 16-board rack opens at about 35 % instead of about 25 %.
- **The USB-serial adapter's jumper wires** run from each pin on the adapter to its pin on the board's header.
- Cables are routed clear of a board's own plugs, and a ribbon can stand off the board's face to clear a header's wire housings.

## Known limits

- The peg fit, crush ribs, the long release rod through a column, the slot for a board nothing clips in, and the tongue under a tall column are all untested in plastic.
- A second J-Link for one board needs a ribbon of about 250 mm (about 360 mm on a rack you have already built); the rack says how long.
- Big racks are slow: a rack of nine boards takes about 10 seconds to build, and the 3D view can stall for a few seconds when you change one.
- The sizes of the newer connector types (SATA, SFP, mini-DIN, C14, XLR, banana, M12, TOSLINK, SIM, small coax, and the mezzanine and card-socket bodies) are typical ones, not from datasheets: check them against your parts. They can be recognised on an imported board but are not in the toolbox yet.
- A card in an M.2, PCIe or DIMM socket isn't drawn, and two boards that mate on a board-to-board connector aren't treated as one stack: put them in a stack by hand.
- Allegro `.brd` import was tested with a stand-in for KiCad's tool, not yet with a real Allegro board.
